The two advisories published since the 2026-07-23 look are N/A: CVE-2026-66061 / GHSA-j23v-9672-677j and CVE-2026-66060 / GHSA-2xqv-hwrf-983f (both HIGH, both 2026-07-31, 'Companion app forwards NFC/QR tag scans to Home Assistant without user confirmation, allowing silent automation execution by untrusted callers') declare ecosystems 'ios' and 'android' with fix versions 2026.5.0 / 2026.5.3 -- COMPANION MOBILE APPS, not the Core container, exactly like CVE-2026-54318 / CVE-2026-55844 / CVE-2026-44698 before them. No Core-server advisory has a fixed version newer than 2026.6.0; REM-094's CVE-2026-54317 stays closed at the pin. THE EXPOSURE IS CONFIGURATION, four facts each read from the RUNNING container: (1) THE ROUTER IS ANONYMOUS -- live GET /api/http/routers shows homeassistant@file, Host(`home.<tld>`), middlewares [security-headers@file, compress@file], NO authentik@file. traefik_auth_modes.homeassistant='oidc' means NATIVE OIDC, which ADDS a Sign-in-with-Authentik button to HA's own login page; it does not put a wall in front of it. POST /auth/login_flow is reachable with no credentials. The 127.0.0.1:8123 host-bind constrains only the direct container port, not the Traefik path. (2) EVERY FAILED LOGIN COSTS A COST-12 BCRYPT -- auth/providers/homeassistant.py:161-178 validate_login hardcodes a dummy $2b$12$ hash and, for an UNKNOWN username, runs bcrypt.checkpw(b'foo', dummy) with the comment 'check a hash to make timing the same as if user was found'. The anti-timing-attack defence IS the amplifier: an invalid username costs exactly as much as a valid one. MEASURED IN-CONTAINER ON THIS HOST: 207.7 ms per checkpw, avg of 5. Container capped at cpus: 1.0. 1000/207.7 = ~4.8 anonymous req/s from ONE client saturate HA's entire CPU allocation. (3) THE BAN THAT WOULD STOP IT IS INERT -- components/http/__init__.py:130 sets ip_ban_enabled default=True, but :128 sets login_attempts_threshold default=NO_LOGIN_ATTEMPT_THRESHOLD = -1 (:96), and ban.py:147 process_wrong_login returns on `if KEY_BAN_MANAGER not in request.app or request.app[KEY_LOGIN_THRESHOLD] < 1: return` -- BEFORE the failed-attempt counter increments and before any ban issues. The enabled-looking ip_ban never fires for login flooding unless a positive threshold is explicitly set. The live /config/configuration.yaml writes an http: block (use_x_forwarded_for + trusted_proxies) and sets NEITHER key. (4) SECOND INDEPENDENT LEG -- ban.py:123 runs `await hass.async_add_executor_job(gethostbyaddr, request.remote)` on every failed attempt, AHEAD of that early return, so each anonymous bad login also occupies a bounded executor thread for a blocking reverse-DNS lookup. Against a source whose PTR stalls, thread-pool occupancy is a cheaper path than the CPU one. AMPLIFIED BY REM-169: no rateLimit and no inFlightReq on this router, so nothing meters the stream before it reaches any of the above. REACHABILITY, stated honestly with the REM-144 caveat: CONFIRMED anonymous from LAN/Tailscale (Traefik binds 0.0.0.0:443; only precondition is host:443 + Host header). INTERNET reach UNVERIFIED and NOT claimed -- split-horizon dnsmasq resolves the name to the host's own LAN address, so a local curl provably never leaves the LAN. Availability-only: nothing read, written or disclosed. Rated HIGH on the same basis as REM-074 (calibre-web ReDoS): unauthenticated, single-client, trivially scripted, and it takes down the home-automation control plane. ACTION in order: (a) set http.login_attempts_threshold to a positive integer (5 is conventional) in the ANSIBLE MANAGED http: block the role already writes into /config/configuration.yaml -- this activates the ip_ban_enabled=True already in force and makes leg (3) real; (b) attach a rateLimit middleware to homeassistant@file, see REM-169 for the estate-wide form; (c) OPTIONAL and SEPARATE: weigh traefik_auth_modes.homeassistant 'oidc' -> 'proxy' so Authentik fronts the login flow, against the Companion apps and webhook/API integrations that would break behind forward-auth -- do NOT flip without checking those consumers. REM-106 VERIFIED CORRECT ON EVIDENCE: `brew list --versions dnsmasq` -> 2.93 installed; `brew info --json=v2 dnsmasq` -> stable 2.93. The host is at upstream's full fix release for the May-2026 CERT/CC cluster (VU#471747; 2.92rel2 hotfix, 2.93 release), clearing CVE-2026-2291 (extract_name heap overflow -> cache poisoning/redirect/DoS) and CVE-2026-5172 (extract_addresses OOB read), on top of the four legs already N/A by config (no dnssec, no dhcp-range, no add-subnet). No repo change was needed: tasks/dnsmasq.yml uses community.general.homebrew state:present, so the host tracked upstream by itself. HOUSEKEEPING: default.config.yml:1720 still says dnsmasq_version '2.91' -- doc-only (nothing consumes it) but it is the only dnsmasq version string in the repo and now under-reports the live host by two releases; advance it to '2.93' so the next scan does not re-derive a closed finding. PROBE (ssrf_vector_analysis) -> REM-154. The managed block in tasks/dnsmasq.yml emits address=, listen-address=, bind-interfaces, local=/<tenant_domain>/ and cache-size -- but NOT `stop-dns-rebind`, and dnsmasq's rebind filter is OFF by default. Since local= scopes authority to the tenant domain only, every other name is forwarded upstream and the answer returned verbatim, including answers pointing into 127.0.0.0/8 or RFC-1918. LIVE-CONFIRMED, not inferred: `dig +short @127.0.0.1 localtest.me A` -> 127.0.0.1 (localtest.me is a public name whose authoritative answer IS 127.0.0.1 -- a safe non-destructive stand-in for an attacker rebinding domain; with stop-dns-rebind dnsmasq would have filtered it). Control `dig +short @1.1.1.1 localtest.me A` -> same answer, confirming relay rather than synthesis. Effective {{homebrew_prefix}}/etc/dnsmasq.conf contains no stop-dns-rebind / rebind-domain-ok / rebind-localhost-ok anywhere (only upstream's commented samples). SCOPE, stated honestly because the obvious over-claim is wrong: dnsmasq binds 127.0.0.1 AND the en0 LAN address (dnsmasq_lan_access defaults TRUE), so it is an unauthenticated forwarding resolver for any LAN/Tailscale client pointed at it -- the documented purpose of that flag. For that population the relay is real. It does NOT chain into this batch's container SSRF findings: Docker containers resolve via Docker's embedded DNS (127.0.0.11) -> Docker Desktop VM upstream, and on the host /etc/resolver/<tenant_domain> is DOMAIN-SCOPED, so mDNSResponder consults dnsmasq only for the tenant domain. dnsmasq is therefore NOT in the resolution path an n8n/metabase rebinding attack would need. Rated EXPLOITABLE for LAN-resolver clients, THEORETICAL as a container-SSRF amplifier; filed because it becomes load-bearing the moment anything is pointed at dnsmasq as a general resolver. IMPACT for the in-scope population: a LAN client browsing an attacker page gets a short-TTL flip to 127.0.0.1/192.168.x, and same-origin policy then treats attacker JS as same-origin with services on THAT client's loopback -- including, on the operator's own workstation, the loopback-bound admin surfaces (portainer 9002, metabase 3002, n8n 5678, alloy 12345) that the rest of this queue treats as protected BY that bind. ACTION: add `stop-dns-rebind` to the managed block, and `rebind-localhost-ok` ALONGSIDE IT -- required, not optional: on a local-TLD install the tenant domain is itself answered as 127.0.0.1 (dnsmasq_dev_address), so a bare stop-dns-rebind would filter nOS's own *.dev.local answers and break the platform by name. Exempt any legitimate private-address domain with rebind-domain-ok=/<domain>/ rather than dropping the guard. Consider documenting dnsmasq_lan_access=false for operators without the guest-device use case. Pin with a tests/anatomy/ gate.

VERBATIM: 'Limit message templates (Template: yes) to 32 KB, limit printf widths and precisions to below 1000, and limit indent/nindent to 100 spaces, preventing excessive memory use from a single small template.' THIS IS THE MEMORY HALF OF A DoS WHOSE CPU HALF nOS ALREADY CARRIES: REM-132 leg (3) recorded v2.26.0's 'Prevent a CPU denial of service via message templates (Template: yes)', which added an execution TIMEOUT. A timeout bounds how LONG a template runs; it does not bound how much it ALLOCATES. The fix names its own amplification primitives -- printf width/precision, indent/nindent -- each of which expands a small request body into an arbitrarily large string before any clock-based cap can fire. The pinned v2.26.3 has the timeout and NOT the allocation cap. Two nOS-specific reasons this matters more than the raw severity suggests: the container is capped at mem_limit 512m (docker_mem_limit_light, default.config.yml:347 -- the SMALLEST tier in the estate), so the ceiling an attacker must reach to trigger an OOM-kill is the lowest of any service; and ntfy is the A9 notification-fanout transport, so OOM-killing it does not merely drop a service, it silently blinds the alerting path that would report the outage. restart: unless-stopped brings it back; the in-flight notifications are gone. v2.27.0 carries a second security item, verbatim with the vendor's own hedge retained: 'Exclude secrets from the config hash served to the web app, preventing a rather theoretical information leak' -- no secret-bearing field is named. SOURCING CAVEAT, now confirmed for the THIRD consecutive ntfy scan and a permanent property of this component: binwiederhier/ntfy's GitHub security-advisories endpoint returns ZERO published advisories, OSV has no ntfy records, NVD has no CVE for any of this. Release-note level only -- do NOT cite a CVE, a GHSA or a vendor CVSS for them. PROBE (resource_exhaustion_vectors) -- ntfy's visitor rate limiting is the ONE limiter in the estate that is correctly wired, and it was VERIFIED BY READING THE SOURCE rather than assumed, because the obvious hypothesis (spoof X-Forwarded-For, get a fresh bucket per request, bypass every per-visitor limit) would have been a serious finding if true. It is not. server.yml.j2 sets behind-proxy: true and leaves proxy-forwarded-header at its X-Forwarded-For default; ntfy v2.26.3 server/util.go extractIPAddressFromHeader documents and implements 'we first remove the trusted IP addresses from the list, and then take the RIGHT-MOST address in the list (as this is the one added by our proxy server)'. Traefik APPENDS the real connecting client to the right of X-Forwarded-For, so the right-most entry is the genuine client and a caller who pre-poisons the header only prepends entries that are never read. proxy-trusted-hosts is empty, which is correct for a single-proxy topology. NOT SPOOFABLE -- recorded as verified-mitigated, not a finding. The per-visitor buckets therefore genuinely hold: visitor-request-limit-burst 60 / replenish 5s, visitor-subscription-limit 30, visitor-attachment-total-size-limit 100M, visitor-attachment-daily-bandwidth-limit 500M (all defaults), plus explicitly-set attachment-file-size-limit 15M and attachment-total-size-limit 5G, cache-duration 12h. attack_probe_schedule.note: Cycle-17 batch-38 FIRST RUN of this probe type, over woodpecker/jellyfin/traefik/uptime_kuma/calibreweb (2026-07-30). All five components were LIVE on the host, so every claim is from an actual unauthenticated HTTP request rather than config inference. 4 items filed (REM-144 CRITICAL, REM-145 HIGH, REM-146 LOW, REM-147 LOW) plus REM-148 from the CVE leg. THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD: looking for leaked version strings surfaced leaked CREDENTIALS. Traefik's own dashboard/API answers anonymously at the edge -- traefik_auth_modes.traefik='none' plus a manifest entry carrying domain_var+port_var means services.yml.j2 derives a websecure router with NO authentik@file, and Traefik then proxies around the very 127.0.0.1:8080 bind that every prior disposition cited as the control. /api/http/middlewares serves rendered customRequestHeaders verbatim, disclosing X-Wing-Edge-Token, X-Face-Edge-Token and -- because face_edge_token is templated as '{{ global_password_prefix }}_pw_face_edge' -- global_password_prefix itself, the seed for every unset '{prefix}_pw_{service}' credential. GENERAL LESSON, the sharper mirror of batch-34's: batch-34 established that auth mode 'oidc' means the edge is open and the app's own login is the only gate; 'none' means the edge is open and there is NO gate -- which for an infrastructure surface with no login of its own is simply an anonymous admin API. A repo gate asserting that no manifest entry with a domain_var maps to auth mode 'none' without an explicit allowlist would have caught this years earlier. SECONDARY PATTERN, the probe's nominal quarry: the services that leak version are exactly the native_oidc ones (woodpecker /version, jellyfin /System/Info/Public + 'Server: Kestrel'), because 'oidc' attaches no edge middleware; the two forward_auth services (uptime_kuma, calibreweb) leaked nothing anonymously -- both 302'd to Authentik. Note also that the security-headers@file middleware strips NO response headers: it only ADDS HSTS/nosniff/XSS/referrer, so any upstream Server or X-Powered-By passes through the edge untouched. --- PRIOR:
